name: 梅もと ヤエチカ店
address_ja: 東京都中央区八重洲2-1 八重洲地下街 北1号　外堀地下2番通り
cuisine: Stand-and-eat station soba in the Yaesu underground arcade — kake soba ¥330, a two-tray mori ¥450–500, the house kakiage-ten soba ¥390, a mini kakiage donburi set ¥550, and, unusually for a soba stall, a shoyu ramen at ¥430; ticket machine at the door, seventeen places, most of them standing
neighborhood: Yaesu 2-chōme, inside Yaechika (the Yaesu underground mall) on Sotobori-chika 2-bandōri — 2 min from the JR Tokyo Station Yaesu North ticket gate, 204 m from the station
gf_detail: Wheat is everywhere and nothing is protected. This is a ¥300–500 station stall with one boiling vat: soba, udon and a shoyu ramen all come out of the same water, so the ramen's wheat noodle alone rules the pot out. The soba is an ordinary cheap-stall blend — no buckwheat ratio is published anywhere, so assume it is heavily cut with wheat flour — the tsuyu is built on ordinary wheat soy sauce, and the signature kakiage is a wheat-batter fritter from a shared fryer that also handles shungiku-ten, korokke and gesoten. There is no allergen chart, no gluten-free item, and no staff time to handle a request: the queue moves in seconds.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is a bonito-and-kaeshi dashi and the ramen broth is chicken-based. Kitsune soba (¥380–390) is plant-based only in its topping; the broth under it is not. No vegan option, and no way to negotiate one at a Japanese-only ticket machine.

roles: brand of ちよだ鮨 (Chiyoda Sushi Co., Ltd.) since 1 October 2022
formerly 株式会社梅もと, 代表取締役社長 宮崎憲昭
chef_bio.origin: Tokyo — founded as a family shop in Meiji 9 (1876); the Yaechika branch is the surviving flagship of the soba chain
chef_bio.background: Honest framing first: this is not a mom-and-pop shop and probably should not be filed as one. Umemoto is one of the older names in Tokyo's cheap-soba trade — an individual business from 1876, incorporated as 合資会社梅もと in 1953 and 株式会社梅もと in 1961, headquartered in Tsukiji, with around 200 staff and a sideline making bentō. It briefly ran a six-shop pizza chain called Pizzateria from about 1970 as an experiment and closed it after five years. The bentō division was sold to Taihei in 2016; the remaining soba business was bought by the take-away sushi chain Chiyoda Sushi, which absorbed 株式会社梅もと outright on 1 October 2022 — the corporation no longer exists and the brand is now run by Chiyoda Sushi, unchanged in name and shopfront. Wikipedia's branch list shows how far the chain has shrunk: of a roster that once ran from Shinjuku and Shibuya to Shinagawa, Kanda, Akihabara and Funabashi, the Yaechika branch is essentially what is left. It opens at 07:15 for the commuter breakfast trade and closes at 21:30, seventeen places, mostly standing, no reservations, no credit cards but IC money and QR payment accepted.
chef_bio.specialty: Kakiage-ten soba ¥390; two-tray mori ¥450–500; a shoyu ramen at ¥430 that regulars rate as highly as the soba; mini kakiage-don set ¥550.

anecdotes.text: Regulars note that showing a JAF membership card gets you a free ō-mori (large portion) — about a ¥60 saving on a ¥450 plate.
Umemoto ran a pizza chain, Pizzateria, for roughly five years from about 1970 — six shops including one in Yaesu — purely as a test bed for know-how, then closed it.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13011518 gives the exact address in the Yaechika arcade, the 07:15/07:30/08:00 opening times by day, 17 seats (standing counter plus 14 stools), all-non-smoking, no reservations, no cards but IC and QR money, and the Chiyoda Sushi homepage link. Japanese Wikipedia's 梅もと article supplies the 1876 founding, the 1953/1961 incorporations, the Tsukiji head office, the ~200 staff, the 2016 bentō sale to Taihei and the 1 October 2022 absorption into Chiyoda Sushi, plus the branch list showing Yaechika as the survivor. Yahoo Japan's place panel corroborates the address, the phone (03-3275-1893) and the menu prices.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One boiling vat serves soba, udon and a wheat-noodle shoyu ramen; the tempura fryer runs continuously through service. There is no wheat-free anything to protect.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard sweet-salty Kantō tsuyu built on ordinary soy sauce. No tamari or wheat-free soy is mentioned anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito-based tsuyu in every bowl; the fryer handles gesoten (squid) and korokke alongside the vegetable kakiage.

positives.text: Practically easy in every non-dietary way: ticket machine, IC and QR payment accepted, all-non-smoking, listed as easy to enter alone, open from 07:15 for breakfast.

cultural_comfort.note: A bright underground stall two minutes inside the Yaesu North gate: buy a ticket at the machine, hand it over, take your tray, stand and eat. No reservation, no waiting for a table, IC card or QR payment accepted, entirely non-smoking. The barrier is language rather than atmosphere — the ticket machine and menu boards are Japanese-only and the queue moves too fast for a conversation, so anyone who has to explain a dietary restriction will find this the wrong kind of place. Lunchtime queues run to about ten people but clear in minutes.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED and pinned. The light record read only 「梅もと」 with a Yaesu / Tokyo Station neighborhood; the branch that matches is 梅もと ヤエチカ店 in the Yaechika underground arcade, and the name has been made specific. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP, but Umemoto is a chain brand now owned and operated by ちよだ鮨 — 株式会社梅もと was absorbed on 1 October 2022 and no longer exists. Suggest recategorising as chain. Coordinates are now exact.

name: とんかつ芝
cuisine: A seven-seat counter tonkatsu shop on Route 15 in Shiba, open since May 2019 — lunch sets ¥1,300–1,500 (hire, rōsu, a hire-and-prawn mix), brand pork including Kamui rib rōsu; the queue starts before 11:30 and the room seats seven
neighborhood: Shiba 4-chōme, Minato-ku, on the Dai-ichi Keihin — 4 min from Toei Mita line Mita station exit A9, 9 min from JR Tamachi's Mita (west) exit, 291 m from Mita station. This is about 2.5 km south of Tokyo Station, NOT Marunouchi.
gf_detail: Tonkatsu is wheat by construction: flour dredge, egg wash, panko crumb, deep-fried in a fryer shared with prawn and chicken katsu. The finishing sauce is a Worcester-style tonkatsu sauce (wheat), the alternative on the counter is soy sauce (wheat), and the miso soup that comes with the set is dashi and miso with no allergen information. Nothing on the menu is gluten-free and no wheat-free preparation is offered.
vegan_detail: A pork-cutlet counter. Shredded cabbage and rice are the only plant items, the fryer is animal territory all service, and the miso soup is bonito dashi. No vegan option exists.

chef_bio.background: Opened 31 May 2019 as a street-level shop on the Dai-ichi Keihin (National Route 15) in Shiba. It briefly ran a second-floor room and has since contracted back to the ground-floor counter alone — seven seats. Diners describe a shop that has held its prices through the recent inflation by quietly swapping the rōsu in the mixed set for chicken rather than raising the number, which regulars read as an act of good faith rather than a downgrade. Lunch is walk-in only; dinner takes reservations. It rates 3.48 on Tabelog across 233 reviews and one regular calls it the best tonkatsu lunch in the Kantō region. No owner name is published, there is no website, and no chain affiliation could be found.
chef_bio.specialty: Hire katsu set; the mixed hire-and-prawn set at roughly ¥1,300–1,500; Kamui-brand rib rōsu.

anecdotes.text: Reviewers note the shop kept its set price unchanged through 2025–26 by substituting chicken for the rōsu in the mixed set — read by regulars as 良心 (conscience) rather than cost-cutting.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13236287 gives the address 港区芝4-5-9, the 2019-05-31 opening, the seven-seat single-floor counter, 11:00-14:00 / 18:00-20:00 hours with Sunday closed, cards and IC/QR payment accepted, and the phone 03-6722-6066. Yahoo Japan's place panel corroborates the address, the hours and the ¥1,300 lunch mix set. No other Japanese source was found, and no shop by any spelling of this name exists in Marunouchi.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Flour, egg and panko station plus a single shared fryer for pork, chicken and prawn. Nothing wheat-free passes through this kitchen.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Tonkatsu sauce and soy sauce are the two condiments on the counter; both are wheat-based. No tamari mentioned.

positives.text: Cards (VISA/Master/JCB/AMEX/Diners), IC money and PayPay are all accepted — unusual for a seven-seat counter.

cultural_comfort.note: Seven seats at a counter, a queue outside from about 11:30, and no English menu found; you order, eat and leave. Cashless payment is accepted, which removes one friction. Come before 11:15 or after 13:15. It is not near Tokyo Station — budget the Mita/Tamachi walk into any plan built around this record.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「とんかつ かつ芝」 in 「中央区 丸の内」. No business called かつ芝 exists anywhere in Japan — a Yahoo Japan exact-phrase search for かつ芝 returns only the place panel for とんかつ芝 plus unrelated 芝海老かつ (shrimp cutlet) hits. とんかつ芝 is a real Tokyo tonkatsu shop and the near-exact name match, so the record has been re-pointed to it. NOTE FOR A HUMAN: this also moves the pin about 2.5 km, from Marunouchi to Shiba 4-chōme in Minato-ku. The light record's own neighborhood string was already self-contradictory (丸の内 is in Chiyoda-ku, not 中央区), which is why the name was trusted over the location. The competing reading is that the sweep meant かつ吉 新丸ビル店, the best-known tonkatsu shop actually in Marunouchi (新丸ビル 5F, bodaijyu.co.jp) — if the pin matters more than the name, that is the record to substitute. Confidence set to medium for that reason.

cuisine: COULD NOT VERIFY — no restaurant called 丸善食堂 exists in Marunouchi or anywhere near Tokyo Station
neighborhood: Unverified. The light record says 中央区 丸の内 — a contradiction in itself, since Marunouchi is in Chiyoda-ku.
gf_detail: Not assessed — the business could not be identified. Note for whoever re-sources this: if the intended entity is Maruzen's own M&C Café, its signature dish is hayashi rice, a roux-thickened Western stew whose base is wheat flour, so the yōshoku framing in the light record would still land on a firm no.
vegan_detail: Not assessed. The light record's 'limited' was inferred from the yōshoku genre label, not from any menu.

chef_bio.background: Could not be established. A Yahoo Japan exact-phrase search for 丸善食堂 returns four distinct businesses, none of them in Marunouchi: 丸善食堂 at 墨田区墨田4-20-1 near Kanegafuchi station in Tokyo (Tabelog 13081557 — a bare listing with no reviews, no published hours and no genre beyond 食堂, phone 03-3612-1224, so nothing about it can honestly be written up); 丸善食堂 in Kadoma, Osaka (an oden shop); 丸善食堂 in Akashi, Hyōgo; and a Sanuki udon 丸善食堂 in Ayagawa, Kagawa, founded in 1972. The likely source of the confusion is the Maruzen bookshop in Marunouchi Oazo, which runs two cafés under its own name — M&C Café on 4F, the shop that claims the invention of hayashi rice by Maruzen's founder Hayashi Yūteki, and Cafe 1869 by MARUZEN on 3F — but neither is called 丸善食堂 and neither is a mom-and-pop. On the evidence available the record is either a garbling of M&C Café or a name generated during the breadth sweep.
chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Yahoo Japan exact-phrase 丸善食堂 (four businesses, none in Marunouchi); Tabelog 13081557 for the Sumida-ku listing, which is a stub; Tabelog 13010996 (M&C Café 丸の内オアゾ) and Tabelog 13215333 (Cafe 1869 by MARUZEN), the two Maruzen-run cafés that do exist in Marunouchi, both corroborated by Marunouchi.com tenant pages.

cultural_comfort.note: Business could not be identified, so nothing can honestly be said.

enrich_note: UNRESOLVED. Yahoo Japan exact-phrase search for 丸善食堂 plus a Marunouchi-scoped search are both negative for the recorded location. The only Tokyo 丸善食堂 is a review-less, hours-less Tabelog stub at 墨田区墨田4-20-1 by Kanegafuchi station (35.731413/139.822239), about 7 km from the pin and nothing like a Marunouchi yōshoku room; the others are in Osaka, Hyōgo and Kagawa. If the sweep meant Maruzen's own Marunouchi café, the real entity is M&C Café 丸の内オアゾ (千代田区丸の内1-6-4 丸の内オアゾ 4F, the hayashi-rice shop, Tabelog 13010996) or Cafe 1869 by MARUZEN on 3F — but those are department-store cafés, not the mom-and-pop this record claims. Coordinates unchanged, loc_precise:false. Candidate for deletion, or for replacement by M&C Café on a human's call.

name: 九頭龍蕎麦 丸ビル店
address_ja: 〒100-6390 東京都千代田区丸の内2-4-1 丸の内ビルディング 6F
cuisine: Fukui country cooking and hand-cut soba on the 6th floor of the Marunouchi Building, looking down on the red brick of Tokyo Station — lunch ¥1,210–1,880 (Echizen oroshi soba with sharp grated daikon, soba with a Fukui sauce-katsu don, prawn tempura zaru); dinner is monthly kaiseki at ¥13,200–18,800 with Echizen crab in season and thirty-plus Fukui sakes
neighborhood: Marunouchi 2-chōme, 6F of the Marunouchi Building — 1 min from Tokyo Station on the JR and Marunouchi lines, 233 m from Nijūbashimae station on the Chiyoda line
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim, and wheat runs through the whole menu. The shop mills and cuts its own soba but publishes no buckwheat ratio anywhere, so the noodle itself cannot be assumed wheat-free — and even a jūwari cut would not be safe here, because a hand-cut board is dusted with uchiko and the tsuyu is a soy-sauce kaeshi (wheat by default; no tamari is mentioned). The named house dishes make it worse: the Fukui sauce-katsu don is a panko-breaded cutlet in a wheat Worcester sauce, the tempura sets are wheat batter from a shared fryer, and the kaiseki courses include fried and simmered dishes seasoned from the same soy base. Treat it as a no.
vegan_detail: Echizen oroshi soba is defined by its dashi — the cold tsuyu poured over grated daikon is bonito-based, and Tabelog's keyword cloud for the shop lists 鰹節 outright. Beyond the noodles the kitchen is built on Fukui seafood: Echizen crab, wakasa-guji, sweet shrimp, abalone, sea urchin, plus Wakasa beef. Sesame tofu and the Takeda abura-age bowl are plant-based on paper but arrive in the same wheat-soy, bonito-dashi seasoning. No vegan set and no plant-based tsuyu.

roles: operating company: 株式会社凛倫林輪
chef_bio.origin: Katsuyama, Fukui Prefecture — the town the Kuzuryū River runs through, which is where the shop's name comes from
chef_bio.background: Kuzuryū Soba is a Fukui restaurant transplanted to Tokyo by a Fukui man. The owner, Mamoru Harasaki, writes on the shop's own site about Katsuyama and the Kuzuryū River — 「町の真ん中を流れる九頭竜川」 — and says that going home and standing in that water is what restores him; the restaurant exists to do the same for people in Tokyo, through Fukui country cooking and oroshi soba. The operating company is 株式会社凛倫林輪. The original shop is in Kagurazaka (新宿区神楽坂3-3), with a second at msb Tamachi and this one, the Marunouchi Building branch, which opened on 5 June 2023; the group is also tied to two restaurants in Fukui itself, うるしや in Echizen city and 古志の国 愛山荘. The Marunouchi room is the dress-up version of the brand: 44 seats over counter, tables, semi-private boxes and full private rooms for up to 12, a view down onto the red brick of Tokyo Station, and one signature private room done in a Taishō-roman mix of stained glass, shōji, coffered ceiling and William Morris fabric. Soba is milled in-house from buckwheat sent directly from Fukui; over thirty Fukui sakes are kept, including rare bottlings of Kokuryū. Lunch is cheap for the address (¥1,210 set, ¥1,380 soba-and-sauce-katsu-don, ¥1,880 prawn tempura zaru); dinner kaiseki changes monthly and runs ¥13,200 for the hairy-crab course up to ¥18,800.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「心を太くする食があります」 — food that thickens the spirit; Fukui's mountain and sea produce cooked to taste of itself, matched to the prefecture's sake.
chef_bio.specialty: Echizen oroshi soba with sharp grated daikon; soba with Fukui-style sauce-katsu don; Echizen crab from the November opening; monthly kaiseki; a Kokuryū-heavy sake list.

anecdotes.text: The owner's note on the shop's site is a homesick one: he writes that every time he returns to Katsuyama the river's harsh and gentle murmur hands him back his energy for the next day, and that the restaurant is an attempt to pass that on.

The private room is a deliberate Taishō-roman pastiche — stained glass, shōji screens, a coffered ceiling and William Morris fabric — chosen because Tokyo Station was Japan's front door in the same era.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kuzuryu-soba.tokyo (the branch's own site) gives the address 〒100-6390 丸の内2-4-1 丸ビル6F, the phone 03-6551-2888, hours 11:00-23:00 Mon-Sat and 11:00-22:00 Sun/holidays with lunch 11:00-14:00, the owner's name and Katsuyama origin, the in-house milling, the private-room design and the related shops in Kagurazaka, Tamachi and Fukui. Tabelog 13285104 confirms the address and coordinates, the 2023-06-05 opening, 44 seats with private rooms, all-non-smoking, the monthly kaiseki prices and the lunch prices, and files the shop under そば・日本料理・日本酒バー. BIZMAPS identifies the operator as 株式会社凛倫林輪.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No buckwheat ratio is published for the house soba, uchiko dusting flour is inherent to hand-cutting, and the same kitchen fries tempura and panko cutlets. Nothing here is protected from wheat.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tsuyu is a soy-sauce kaeshi and the kaiseki simmered dishes come from the same base. No tamari or wheat-free soy is mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi in the oroshi tsuyu; the menu is otherwise Fukui seafood — crab, guji, sweet shrimp, abalone, urchin — and Wakasa beef.

positives.text: The shop's own site is published in English as well as Japanese, and the room is all non-smoking with cards, IC money and six QR payment schemes accepted.

cultural_comfort.note: A comfortable door for a visitor: 6F of the Marunouchi Building, a minute from Tokyo Station, open 11:00 to 23:00 every day with no closing day, English pages on the shop's own site, all non-smoking, every card and payment app accepted, and staff who by review accounts enjoy explaining Fukui to outsiders. Lunch is walk-in and cheap for the address; dinner is a booking and a proper kaiseki price. Private rooms for 4, 6 and up to 12.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED and pinned; the light record's name was already correct. Hours as given are the shop's own; Tabelog lists them half an hour later (11:00-22:30 / 11:00-21:30), so the earlier close has been used. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP — it is owner-founded and Fukui-rooted, but 株式会社凛倫林輪 now runs three Tokyo branches plus two Fukui restaurants, so 'small group' is more accurate than mom-and-pop.

name: dancyu食堂
address_ja: 〒100-0005 東京都千代田区丸の内1-9-1 東京駅 グランスタ八重北 1F 八重北食堂
cuisine: The food magazine dancyu's own canteen inside Tokyo Station — teishoku by day, a drinking shokudō by night: ginger pork ¥1,580, pork shūmai ¥1,380, horse-mackerel fry with house tartare ¥1,480, karaage ¥1,480, a yanagawa set ¥1,780, or a ¥1,180 plate of small dishes; 26 seats, twenty of them at the counter, no reservations, 11:00–23:00
neighborhood: Marunouchi 1-9-1, on the Yaekita Shokudō floor of GRANSTA Yaekita, outside the JR Tokyo Station Yaesu North ticket gate — 1–3 min from the gate, 160 m from the station
hours_raw: 11:00 - 23:00（L.O. 料理22:00／小皿・豆皿・ドリンク22:30）　定休日：無休（施設に準ずる）
gf_detail: A Japanese teishoku kitchen with no gluten-free provision at all. The headline dishes are wheat by construction: shūmai in a wheat wrapper, aji-fry and karaage in flour and breadcrumb from a shared fryer, ginger pork in a soy-and-mirin marinade, yanagawa simmered in a soy broth. Soy sauce is on every table and in every seasoning, and no tamari is mentioned. The small-dish plate (¥1,180) is the only route to anything simple, and even there the dressings and simmering liquids are wheat-soy. No allergen chart is published.
vegan_detail: Everything is built on dashi, and the menu is explicitly proud of its fish and meat — aji-fry, buri katsu, shūmai, karaage. Tabelog files the shop as 野菜料理にこだわる alongside 魚料理にこだわる, so there are real vegetable side dishes, but they are seasoned with bonito dashi and wheat soy sauce and there is no vegan set. Treat it as a no.

roles: produced by the food magazine dancyu (President Inc.)
chef_bio.origin: Tokyo Station — opened 27 April 2022 with the first phase of GRANSTA Yaekita
chef_bio.background: This is a magazine's restaurant rather than a family's. dancyu, President Inc.'s food monthly, announced in January 2022 that it would open its first ever produced restaurant inside JR Tokyo Station, and dancyu食堂 opened on 27 April 2022 with the first phase of GRANSTA Yaekita, on the Yaekita Shokudō floor just outside the Yaesu North gate. The brief the magazine set itself is deliberately unglamorous: lunch is teishoku, evening is a 呑める食堂 — a canteen you can drink in — and the stated ambition is food you would want to eat every day rather than food you photograph, with the sourcing story of each ingredient and each sake told alongside it. In practice that means a 26-seat room, twenty of the seats at the counter, no reservations, a lunch queue that regulars warn about, and prices in the ¥1,180–1,780 band that read as high for a station canteen and reasonable for what arrives. It rates 3.49 on Tabelog across 1,094 reviews, the top-ranked 食堂 in Marunouchi, and dancyu went on to found a dancyu 総合研究所 in 2023 off the back of it. No individual chef is credited publicly.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「昼は定食メイン、夜は“吞める食堂”」 — ordinary, genuinely good food and snacks, served with the story of where the ingredient and the sake came from.
chef_bio.specialty: Ginger pork teishoku ¥1,580; pork shūmai teishoku ¥1,380; aji-fry with house tartare ¥1,480; the ¥1,180 kobachi (small-dish) teishoku; a short sake and wine list for the evening.

anecdotes.text: dancyu announced the shop in January 2022 as the magazine's first ever produced restaurant; it opened on 27 April 2022 with the first phase of GRANSTA Yaekita.
Reviewers repeatedly warn that the shop is hard to find because it sits underground where phone GPS fails, and that the tartare sauce with the aji-fry makes the bottled sauce on the table redundant.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13271151 gives the address inside GRANSTA Yaekita, the coordinates, the 2022-04-27 opening, 26 seats (20 counter), no reservations, 11:00-23:00 with no closing day, all-non-smoking, children welcome, and the priced menu. dancyu.jp and gransta.jp carry the shop's own description of the 昼定食 / 夜吞める食堂 concept and confirm it is the magazine's first produced restaurant; president.co.jp's January 2022 release announced the opening; PR TIMES repeats the April 2022 date in its 2023 dancyu 総合研究所 announcement.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Aji-fry, karaage and buri katsu share one fryer, and shūmai wrappers are wheat. There is no wheat-free item to protect.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Ginger pork marinade, yanagawa broth, the dressings on the small dishes and the bottled sauce on the table are all wheat-soy or Worcester-style. No tamari mentioned.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi underlies the vegetable side dishes; the menu is otherwise pork and fish.

positives.text: All non-smoking, children welcome, every card and payment app accepted, open 11:00–23:00 with no closing day — a useful fallback at an awkward hour.

cultural_comfort.note: A bright 26-seat counter canteen inside Tokyo Station, open continuously from 11:00 to 23:00 every day of the year, all non-smoking, children welcome, all cards and QR apps accepted. Two frictions: no reservations and a serious lunch queue (arrive before 11:30 or after 13:30), and the shop is hard to find because it sits underground on the Yaekita Shokudō floor where phone GPS stops working — follow the signs from the Yaesu North gate rather than the map. Solo diners are the norm.

enrich_note: CONFIRMED and pinned; the light record's name was correct. CATEGORY FLAG: filed as MOM_AND_POP, but this is a restaurant produced by dancyu magazine (President Inc.) inside a JR East station mall — suggest recategorising as a brand/corporate record. Coordinates are now exact.

name: 十割蕎麦酒場 ちゃぼうず 大手町店
address_ja: 〒100-0005 東京都千代田区丸の内1-1-3 日本生命丸の内ガーデンタワー 2F
cuisine: A soba izakaya on the 2nd floor of the Nippon Life Marunouchi Garden Tower: house-milled jūwari soba from 100% domestic buckwheat, boiled only once the order is in, alongside sashimi platters, jidori chicken grilled in soba-miso and shabu-shabu courses from ¥3,850 — lunch about ¥1,000, dinner about ¥4,500, weekdays only
neighborhood: Marunouchi 1-1-3, 2F of the Nippon Life Marunouchi Garden Tower — 1 min from Ōtemachi station exit D6 (Chiyoda line), about 2 min from exit D4, 5 min on foot from Tokyo Station
gf_detail: This is exactly the trap the jūwari label sets. The noodle is 100% domestic buckwheat, milled in the shop, cut in the shop and boiled to order — and that still does not make it gluten-free. Hand-cut soba is worked on a board dusted with uchiko, and nothing the shop publishes says that dusting flour is buckwheat rather than wheat. More decisively, the shop's stated point of pride is a kaeshi made with 本格木桶仕込みの醤油 — barrel-brewed soy sauce, which is wheat by default and is named nowhere as a wheat-free tamari. That kaeshi is in the tsuyu, so it is in every bowl. Around it sits a full izakaya menu with fried dishes from a shared kitchen. No gluten-free claim is made anywhere, and none should be inferred from 十割.
vegan_detail: The soba tsuyu is a dashi-and-kaeshi build, and the kitchen's centre of gravity is sashimi platters, jidori chicken and pork or duck shabu-shabu courses. Sobagaki and the soba-miso are plant-based in principle but arrive as accompaniments to animal dishes and are seasoned from the same base. No vegan course, no plant-based tsuyu, nothing published about substitutions.

roles: second concept ('新業態') of the Ginza shop 酒菜庵 ちゃぼうず
part of a multi-brand Tokyo restaurant group
chef_bio.origin: Ginza — the parent shop 酒菜庵 ちゃぼうず; this branch is in Ōtemachi
chef_bio.background: Chabōzu began in Ginza as 酒菜庵 ちゃぼうず, and this Ōtemachi shop is described by the group as the brand's new format: a soba izakaya rather than a soba restaurant, on the second floor of the Nippon Life Marunouchi Garden Tower, connected to Ōtemachi station and five minutes from Tokyo Station. The soba is the anchor — 国産そば粉100％の自家製十割, ground in-house and boiled only once the order is placed, which is the detail reviewers keep returning to — but the business is built for the office district around it: 36 seats over sofa and counter, private hire from 30 people, banquet courses from ¥3,850, two-and-a-half-hour free-flow options including an all-you-can-drink Dassai upgrade, no otōshi cover charge and no table charge, and a shutter that comes down entirely at the weekend. The operator runs a spread of unrelated brands alongside it — 一軒炉端 とうきち, しゃぶの湯, 其レハサテオキ, 円山荘, 博多・串 ヒロシチャン, 台灣夜市101 — so this is a group restaurant with a craft claim rather than a soba master's shop. No chef is named publicly.
chef_bio.philosophy: Jūwari soba from 100% domestic buckwheat, milled in-house and boiled to order, with a kaeshi from barrel-fermented soy sauce; the soba shop as a place to drink.
chef_bio.specialty: 十割盛り蕎麦; sashimi platters; jidori chicken grilled with soba-miso; pork and duck shabu-shabu courses; a sake list running to Dassai 45.

anecdotes.text: A 2026 reviewer records the working detail that the shop grinds its own 100% domestic buckwheat and only puts the noodles in water once the order is placed — the reason the lunch service runs slower than an office district usually tolerates.
The group waives both the otōshi cover charge and any table charge, which is unusual for an izakaya in this postcode.

roles: brand of 株式会社シナジー (Synergy Inc.), founded 2006
chef_bio.origin: Ōtemachi, Tokyo — one branch of a multi-city restaurant company
chef_bio.background: Honest framing first: this is a corporate brand, not a mom-and-pop. 石楽 is one of the restaurant concepts of 株式会社シナジー, a company founded in 2006 that by its own account runs 46 restaurants across Tokyo, Kanagawa, Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Hakata and Vietnam, spanning hand-cut soba (そばしき), tempura, unagi and hitsumabushi (和牛ひつまぶし 六重亭), Italian and Spanish. Synergy markets this concept in full as 石臼挽き二八そば 石楽 — stone-milled nihachi soba — and runs sibling branches at MARK IS Minatomirai and JOINUS Yokohama. The Ōtemachi shop sits in the basement restaurant street of the Ōtemachi Park Building, connected directly to the station, and is built around the weekday office lunch: 48 seats over tables and counter, a warm wood room, private hire for 20 to 50, and a day that runs unbroken from 11:00 to 23:00 on weekdays and shuts entirely at the weekend. Reviewers describe the lunch as reliably good rather than remarkable — a soba-and-donburi set at ¥1,350–1,430 — and note that the building's basement is a genuine maze. No chef is credited.
chef_bio.philosophy: Stone-milled nihachi soba paired with tempura, run as an all-day soba izakaya for an office district.
chef_bio.specialty: Tendon with mori soba ¥1,350; bonito zuke-don with soba ¥1,430; oyster nanban soba ¥1,650; whitebait donburi sets; evening courses with free-flow drinks.

anecdotes.text: Reviewers repeatedly warn that Ōtemachi's basement is its own dungeon — four Tokyo Metro lines crossing on different levels — and that finding the shop is harder than eating in it.

name: 五代目 野田岩 日本橋高島屋特別食堂
address_ja: 〒103-0027 東京都中央区日本橋2-4-1 日本橋髙島屋 本館8F 特別食堂
cuisine: The Azabu unagi house Nodaiwa, serving from a counter inside Nihonbashi Takashimaya's grand old Tokubetsu Shokudō — unaju from ¥4,840, a shirayaki-and-unaju set around ¥8,000, set menus near ¥9,900 including the 10% service charge, eaten in a quiet 164-seat department-store dining room shared with the Imperial Hotel and Yamatoya Sangen counters
neighborhood: Nihonbashi 2-chōme, 8F of the Nihonbashi Takashimaya main building — directly above Nihombashi station exit B1 (Ginza, Tōzai and Asakusa lines), 192 m from the station and about a 7-minute walk from Tokyo Station's Yaesu side
gf_detail: There is no gluten-free claim and no allergen sheet, and the default order is not safe: kabayaki tare is soy sauce and mirin reduced together — wheat by default — brushed on repeatedly over the grill, and the kimosui and pickles that come with the unaju are seasoned from the same soy base. The one thing worth asking about is that Nodaiwa does serve shirayaki, eel grilled plain with no tare, taken with salt and wasabi; this branch lists 白焼きとうな重 at about ¥8,000. That is a starting point rather than an answer — the same grill and the same brushes carry tare all service, prepared wasabi is often thickened, and nothing published says the kitchen will run a separated preparation. This is table service inside a department store with staff who will take the question seriously, so raise it when booking; do not walk in assuming. Recorded as 'ask' rather than 'no' only because shirayaki exists and there is someone to ask.
vegan_detail: An eel specialist. The rice arrives under eel, the soup is made from eel liver, and the counter has no plant-based dish. If a vegan is in the party, the Tokubetsu Shokudō's other counters (the Imperial Hotel's Western menu, Yamatoya Sangen's Japanese one) sit in the same room and are worth checking instead — but nothing at Nodaiwa itself works.

chef_bio.origin: Azabu-Iikura, Minato-ku — the main house is at 東麻布1-5-4
chef_bio.background: Nodaiwa is one of the old Tokyo unagi houses: reviewers and the shop alike put the founding at roughly two hundred years ago in the late Edo period, and the fifth-generation master, Kanejirō Kanemoto, is the man the name is attached to — the Azabu-Iikura main shop trades as 五代目 野田岩 and has carried a Michelin star. The Azabu house's practice is the Tokyo one: the eel is split down the back, skewered, grilled, steamed, then grilled again through the tare, which is what gives Tokyo eel its soft, rendered texture, and Nodaiwa is particularly associated with insisting on natural rather than farmed eel when the season allows — the main shop's menu carries a 天然鰻 supplement. The house also keeps the old rule of closing on the Day of the Ox, the single day of the year the rest of the trade sells eel hardest. What sits inside Nihonbashi Takashimaya is not a branch in the usual sense but a counter in the store's Tokubetsu Shokudō — a formal 164-seat dining room where three famous kitchens serve to the same floor: Nodaiwa for eel, the Imperial Hotel for Western food, and Yamatoya Sangen for Japanese. Takashimaya has confirmed there is no dress code. Prices start at ¥4,840 for unaju and a 10% service charge is added at lunch as well as dinner; at peak eel season the wait for a table has been reported at three and a half hours, taken by leaving a phone number and going shopping.
chef_bio.philosophy: Edo-style unagi — split at the back, skewered, grilled, steamed, grilled again — with a restrained, not-sweet tare; natural eel where the season permits.
chef_bio.specialty: Unaju in the traditional grades (桔梗 / 萩 / 山吹, roughly ¥3,700–5,300 at the main house, from ¥4,840 here); shirayaki, plain-grilled with no tare; the shirayaki-plus-unaju set around ¥8,000; kimosui.

anecdotes.text: The Azabu main house closes on the Day of the Ox in midsummer — the busiest eel-eating day in the Japanese year — which the trade reads as a statement about queues and quality.
A 2026 visitor arriving at 11:30 in eel season was quoted a three-and-a-half-hour wait, left a phone number and went shopping in the store until called.
Takashimaya has confirmed on the record that the Tokubetsu Shokudō, for all its formality, has no dress code.

Listed as barrier-free with wide, well-spaced seating, private rooms available and all non-smoking; a shirayaki (no-tare) dish is on the menu at about ¥8,000.

Two practical traps. Cards: Tabelog lists Diners as the only credit card accepted, though IC money and QR payments are taken — carry cash. Hours differ between sources — Takashimaya's own page says 11:00–20:00 with last orders at 19:00, Tabelog says 21:30/20:00 — so treat 19:00 as the safe last-order time and confirm by phone. Prices carry a 10% service charge at lunch as well as dinner.

name: わんぱく
address_ja: 〒103-0028 東京都中央区八重洲2-8-10 松岡八重洲ビル 1F
cuisine: An unmarked morning standing-soba counter in a Yaesu office block, run by two men — kake soba ¥280, kisu-ten (sand-borer tempura) soba ¥430, aji-ten soba ¥430, the tempura fried in front of you and laid out on a tray on the counter with onigiri and inari; cash only, five or six people fit, shut by four in the afternoon
neighborhood: Yaesu 2-chōme, at the southern end near Kyōbashi — 1 min from Kyōbashi station exit 3b on the Tokyo Metro Ginza line, 167 m from the station, roughly a 7-minute walk south from Tokyo Station's Yaesu side
hours_raw: 7:00〜16:00（Yahoo!マップの利用者報告による。食べログには営業時間の記載なし）　定休日：不明
gf_detail: A ¥280-a-bowl standing counter with one pot and one fryer. The soba is a cheap-stall blend with no published buckwheat ratio — assume it is heavily cut with wheat flour — soba and udon share the boiling water, the tsuyu is ordinary wheat soy sauce, and the whole point of the shop is wheat-battered tempura fried on the spot and stacked in the open on the counter. There is no allergen information, no English, no gluten-free item, and no realistic way to ask: the queue is standing and the shop's own listing bans photography.
vegan_detail: The tsuyu is bonito dashi and the tempura the shop is known for is fish — kisu (sand borer) and aji (horse mackerel) — fried in oil shared with everything else. Inari-zushi on the counter is the only plant item and it is not a meal. Treat it as a no.

roles: owner-operator plus one — described by regulars as two men about a generation apart working the counter together
chef_bio.background: This is the real thing in a district that has very little of it left: a standing-soba counter tucked into the ground floor of the Matsuoka Yaesu Building in a canyon of Yaesu offices, with no shop sign at all — regulars say you find it by the そば・うどん banner outside, with the doorway opposite. Five or six people fill the room and it still generates a queue. It opens at seven in the morning for the commuter breakfast trade and is finished by about four in the afternoon. Two men run it, described by one long-standing regular as a pair roughly a parent and child's age apart, and the draw is the tempura: fried in front of you and laid out on a tray on the counter alongside onigiri and inari, so you order by looking. The kisu-ten is what people come back for — a small piece of sand-borer tempura at about ¥120 on top of a ¥280 kake, which reviewers call absurd value for the postcode. Cash only: no cards, no IC money, no QR payment. The phone number is unlisted, there is no website, and photography inside is prohibited, which is why so little of the shop appears online. Tabelog rates it 3.4 over 175 reviews; Retty 3.9 over 27.
chef_bio.specialty: Kisu-ten soba ¥430; aji-ten soba ¥430; kake soba ¥280; kisu-ten alone about ¥120; curry soba; onigiri and inari on the counter.

anecdotes.text: There is no sign. Regulars describe finding it by the そば・うどん banner outside with the entrance opposite — five people fill the room and a queue still forms.
Photography inside is prohibited — the Tabelog listing carries the shop's own notice 「店内全て撮影禁止です」 — which is unusual enough to be worth knowing before you raise a phone.
A regular writing in 2015 describes the counter being worked by two men roughly a parent and child's age apart, with the tempura as the shop's whole appeal.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13114608 gives the address 中央区八重洲2-8-10 松岡八重洲ビル1F, the coordinates, standing-counter-only seating, no reservations, cash only (no cards, no e-money, no QR), an unlisted phone, takeaway available, the photography ban and a budget under ¥999; it lists no opening hours at all. Yahoo Japan's place panel supplies the 7:00–16:00 hours from user reports along with the ¥430 kisu-ten and aji-ten soba prices. Retty and reviewer blogs supply the room size (five to seven standing), the two-man operation and the counter tray of tempura, onigiri and inari.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One pot for soba and udon, one fryer running fish tempura all morning, and battered pieces sitting open on a tray on the counter. Nothing is separated.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Standard Kantō stall tsuyu on ordinary wheat soy sauce; no tamari, and no allergen information of any kind is published.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Bonito dashi tsuyu; the house tempura is kisu and aji, fried in shared oil.

positives.text: Takeaway is possible, which is the only realistic way to slow the transaction down.

cultural_comfort.note: Rewarding but genuinely demanding. There is no sign on the building — look for the そば・うどん banner on Yaesu 2-chōme near Kyōbashi station exit 3b and the doorway opposite. Inside are five or six standing places, no menu in English, no published phone number, cash only (cards, IC cards and QR payment are all refused), and a posted ban on photography. Ordering is done by pointing at the tempura tray on the counter. Morning only — it opens at 07:00 and is done by about 16:00, and those hours are crowd-reported rather than published, so treat them as approximate. Go early, bring coins, do not raise a camera, and do not expect to be able to hold a conversation about ingredients.

This one really is a mom-and-pop — two men, no sign, no phone, cash only.
